This article analyzes the proportion of steroid courses administered to [[ibd|IBD]] patients over the age of 50 who subsequently received a [[dexa-scanning|DEXA-scanning]], a critical measure for monitoring bone density in patients on long-term steroid therapy. The data evaluates performance at the national, regional, and departmental levels against a stated development target of ≥80% [^src1].

Nationally, the indicator stands at just 37% (338 out of 917 steroid courses), meaning the country as a whole falls significantly short of the ≥80% target [^src1]. In fact, no region or individual department successfully meets this threshold [^src1]. Among the five regions, Sjælland performs best at 41%, followed closely by Hovedstaden (39%) and Syddanmark (38%), while Midtjylland (31%) and Nordjylland (32%) trail behind [^src1]. 

At the departmental level, the highest compliance rates are found at HOL Holbæk Medicin (58%) and Bornholm Medicinsk Afdeling (56%) [^src1]. However, these leading departments are notable outliers operating with very small patient cohorts; Bornholm's percentage is based on just 9 total cases, and Holbæk on 26 [^src1]. Conversely, the lowest performing departments are AAUH Farsø Medicinsk Afdeling at 7% and Aarhus Lever-, Mave- og Tarmsygd. at 11%, both of which also have masked or very small denominators [^src1]. Other notably low performers with larger cohorts include Hvidovre Gastroenheden (20%) and SUH Køge Medicin (26%) [^src1]. 

Because this dataset represents a single cross-sectional snapshot from 2024, no longitudinal trends regarding improvement or decline can be established from this table alone.
